parole.testo: Pseudo-Italianism, constructed from Italian pippione (“squab, young pigeon”) and -olo (diminutive), the former from Latin pīpiōnem (“squab, young pigeon”), ultimately onomatopoeic.
Pseudo-Italianism, derived from the Italian phrase testa di ferro (“iron head”). Compare Asturian testaferru, Leonese testaferre, and Portuguese testa de ferro.
